facts.statement: The genus Psephoderma was described by Meyer in 1858.
facts.quote: authority: Meyer, 1858

facts.statement: Psephoderma lived during the Late Triassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Triassic

facts.statement: The name Psephoderma translates to "pebbly skin" derived from Ancient Greek words.
facts.quote: Psephoderma (meaning "pebbly skin", from the Ancient Greek psepho (ψῆφος), "pebbly", and derma (δέρμα), "skin")

facts.statement: Psephoderma possessed a flattened skull with a narrow, straight snout that was significantly narrower than those of related genera.
facts.quote: Psephoderma had a flattened skull and a narrow, straight rostrum, much narrower than that of its relatives.

facts.statement: Psephoderma had rounded teeth embedded in its jaws that were specialized for crushing shellfish.
facts.quote: Inside this skull, embedded in the jaws, were rounded teeth specialized for crushing the shellfish it ate.

facts.statement: Unlike other placodonts, the carapace of Psephoderma consisted of two separate parts: one covering the shoulders and back, and another covering the ventral end.
facts.quote: Unlike henodontid placodonts, Psephoderma's carapace was divided into two pieces, one on the shoulders and back, and another on the ventral end.

facts.statement: Psephoderma was one of the final placodont genera to exist.
facts.quote: It was one of the last placodonts to live.

facts.statement: Fossils of Psephoderma were discovered in Rhaetian deposits in the Alps and England, which influenced the naming of its species.
facts.quote: Fossils of Psephoderma have been found in the Rhaetian deposits in the Alps and in England, hence the specific names.

facts.statement: The long, narrow snout of Psephoderma featured paired internal grooves leading to the nostrils, a key diagnostic trait for the genus.
facts.quote: This rostrum bore paired grooves on the inside of the mouth, which led to the internal nares and are a diagnostic feature for the genus.

facts.statement: The nasal bones of Psephoderma were extremely small, described as mere splinters of bone.
facts.quote: The nasal bones were very small, mere splinters of bone.

facts.statement: Psephoderma had large, irregularly shaped orbits indicating its eyes were positioned on top of its head to look upwards.
facts.quote: The orbits were large and somewhat irregularly shaped, and indicate that the eyes were on top of the head looking upwards.

facts.statement: The entire skull of Psephoderma was highly compressed from top to bottom.
facts.quote: The whole skull was highly ventrodorsally compressed.

facts.statement: The species P. alpinum possessed elongated, posterior tooth-bearing plates used for crushing its diet of shellfish.
facts.quote: The P. alpinum species had decidedly elongated, posterior, tooth-bearing plates for crushing the shellfish that formed its diet.

facts.statement: Psephoderma lacked teeth on the front of its mouth but had four crushing teeth on each side of the palate, with the fourth tooth being significantly larger than the first three.
facts.quote: No teeth were present along the premaxillae or the rostral area of the maxillae, but four crushing teeth were in each side of the palate, the first three in a triangle of small, rounded teeth and the fourth a short distance behind them.

facts.statement: The absence of front teeth suggests Psephoderma used its elongated snout to dig up shellfish, which were then crushed by large teeth at the back of the mouth.
facts.quote: The lack of teeth near the front of the mouth and rostrum indicate that the elongated rostrum was mainly used for rooting out or digging up shellfish, which would then be taken into the back of the mouth and crushed by the large teeth.

facts.statement: Psephoderma had a deeply excavated occiput and a very small braincase, though the walls of the braincase were thick and well-armored.
facts.quote: Its occiput was deeply excavated and its entire braincase very small. However, the braincase walls were quite thick and well armoured.

facts.statement: Both sections of Psephoderma's carapace were composed of partially fused scutes that were roughly hexagonal or circular in shape.
facts.quote: Both parts of the carapace were made of partially fused scutes, roughly hexagonal or circular in shape.

facts.statement: Psephoderma had a long tail reaching up to 80 cm in length, covered in scutes from base to tip.
facts.quote: Its tail was quite long, up to about 80 cm, and had scutes all the way down it.

facts.statement: Psephoderma's limbs were relatively small paddle-like structures equipped with individual toes rather than flippers.
facts.quote: The limbs were relatively small and would have been used as paddles, but had individual toes rather than a flipper.

facts.statement: Psephoderma is classified within the order Placodontia.
facts.quote: ordo: Placodontia

facts.statement: Psephoderma belongs to the family Placochelyidae.
facts.quote: familia: Placochelyidae

facts.statement: The genus authority for Psephoderma is Meyer, 1858.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Meyer, 1858

facts.statement: The known species of Psephoderma include P. alpinum, the type species, and P. anglicum described by Meyer in 1867.
facts.quote: subdivision: P. alpinum (tipo) P. anglicum Meyer, 1867

facts.statement: The parent group for the genus Psephoderma is Placochelyida.
facts.quote: Parent group: Placochelyida

facts.statement: Psephoderma is classified within the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

rejected.statement: Psephoderma could grow up to 180 cm in length, making it larger than many of its relatives, and lived approximately 210 million years ago.
rejected.quote: Psephoderma grew to 180 cm long, larger than many of its relatives, and lived in the Late Triassic (Norian - Rhaetian), about 210 million years ago.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'larger than many of its relatives and lived'

rejected.statement: The carapace of Psephoderma consisted of two parts: one covering the rib cage and thorax, and the other covering the pelvis.
rejected.quote: The carapace of Psephoderma was made up of two parts, one of which covered the rib cage and thorax and the other of which covered the pelvis.
